Class SlowQueryReportJmx

java.lang.Object
org.apache.tomcat.jdbc.pool.JdbcInterceptor
org.apache.tomcat.jdbc.pool.interceptor.AbstractCreateStatementInterceptor
org.apache.tomcat.jdbc.pool.interceptor.AbstractQueryReport
org.apache.tomcat.jdbc.pool.interceptor.SlowQueryReport
org.apache.tomcat.jdbc.pool.interceptor.SlowQueryReportJmx
All Implemented Interfaces:
InvocationHandler, NotificationBroadcaster, NotificationEmitter, SlowQueryReportJmxMBean
public class SlowQueryReportJmx extends SlowQueryReport implements NotificationEmitter, SlowQueryReportJmxMBean
JMX-enabled slow query report interceptor. Publishes slow and failed query statistics to JMX and provides notifications when slow or failed queries are detected.

With notifyPool=false this interceptor registers its own MBean and broadcaster. In the default notifyPool=true mode it registers nothing and raises notifications on the pool's own MBean instead. The MBean belongs to a pool and is published by the first borrow under the name the pool started with; the publication is attempted once and given up by the pool's close. Names must be unique among live pools.

The published resource is a SlowQueryReportJmx.Registration holding the pool name, the statistics store and the pool's JMX state, but not the pool itself, so an abandoned pool is not pinned by the MBean server. Listener subscriptions belong to the registration they were added through and must be re-attached after a pool closes.

      public static final String SLOW_QUERY_NOTIFICATION
      Notification type for slow query events. The pool's own MBean reports the same event under the same type when this interceptor is configured with notifyPool=true, so this is that very type and not a copy of its text: a client filters notifications on the type, and the two channels have to answer to one string.

    • getNotificationSource

      protected Object getNotificationSource()
      Returns the source this MBean's notifications are sent with.

      Notification marshals its source, so a listener outside this JVM - one reached through a JMX connector, or one that hands the notification on to another process - only receives the notification at all if the source is serializable. This MBean is not, and neither is the pool it reports on, so the source is the ObjectName the MBean is registered under, which names the pool and is serializable. Interceptor instances are created per pooled connection and none of them is the published resource - that is the pool's SlowQueryReportJmx.Registration - so an instance cannot name itself: the source is the ObjectName the pool's JMX state records as published, which every instance of the pool sends alike. That includes the instances of a second definition on one pool: the two-thresholds configuration publishes one MBean, and an instance that published nothing must not stamp its notifications with the name its own properties would compute - that name is registered under nothing, and a client filtering or grouping by source reads the published one. An instance whose name cannot be formed - a malformed objectName property or a pool name that cannot be quoted into an ObjectName - was never registered at all, so no listener reached through a connector can exist for it; the source is then a string of the default name's shape, which still names the pool for the local listeners the broadcaster serves. A pool that carries no name is the same case taken to its end: it holds no registration to name itself by, and the shape its source takes is the default one with no name in it - whatever survives delivery, it cannot name a pool that never had a name to register.

      Returns:
      the ObjectName this interceptor's pool is published under, or, when nothing is published for it or the published name cannot be told, a name formed from this instance - as an ObjectName where that succeeds, and as a string of the default name's shape where it does not

    • setNotifyPool

      public void setNotifyPool(boolean notifyPool)
      Sets whether notifications are sent to the pool. Configuration entry point only, applied to every interceptor instance of a pool by setProperties while its connection chain is built: it is not part of the JMX management interface, because writing it through the registered MBean would reach only the one instance that owns the registration and leave the pool's other connections routing as before. See SlowQueryReportJmxMBean.
      Parameters:
      notifyPool - true if notifications should be sent to the pool

    • resetStats

      public void resetStats()
      JMX operation - remove all stats for this connection pool. The statistics belong to this interceptor's pool, so what this clears is what that pool has recorded - and nothing another pool collected, however it was named. Only the recorded content goes: the statistics store stays registered with the pool, which keeps accumulating into it.
      Specified by:
      resetStats in interface SlowQueryReportJmxMBean

    • registerJmx

      protected void registerJmx()
      Registers this pool's MBean with JMX. The publication is attempted once per pool by the first borrow that needs it; a refusal is logged and not retried. A pool with no statistics store, or whose store has been released, has nothing to publish.

    • setProperties

      public void setProperties(Map<String, PoolProperties.InterceptorProperty> properties)
      Sets the interceptor properties, including the notifyPool flag.

      The flag is read the way the inherited properties are: a value that states neither true nor false is reported and leaves the flag as it stands, rather than being read as the false the raw parser answered with - which would have moved the pool's notifications off the route its default selects without saying so.
